description: Virgo zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (August 23 to September 22).
answer: In Western astrology, Virgo is the sixth sign of the zodiac, a mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury. It is traditionally associated with precision, helpfulness, practical intelligence and a love of improvement. The Sun is in Virgo from about August 23 to September 22.

sections.heading: Virgo personality traits
paragraphs: Virgo is the zodiac's craftsperson and analyst, the sign that spots the loose thread and quietly mends it. Its symbol, the Maiden holding a sheaf of wheat, links it to the harvest: the careful business of sorting, refining and preparing what has grown so that it can nourish others. People with strong Virgo placements tend to find meaning in being useful. They often have a sharp eye for detail, an orderly mind and a sincere wish to make things work better, whether a spreadsheet, a recipe, a daily routine or a friend's tangled problem. Modesty is common, and so is a hidden, very dry wit.

Virgo is a mutable earth sign ruled by Mercury. Earth grounds it in the practical world of bodies, work and material results; mutable signs adapt and refine, which explains the knack for adjusting systems until they run smoothly. Mercury, planet of intellect and communication, here turns its attention to analysis, health, craft and everyday tasks rather than abstract theory. The combination describes a mind that thinks in order to improve and a heart that expresses care through service. Traditionally the sign governs health, routine and daily work, reflecting a quiet conviction that small habits, done well, shape the quality of a whole life.

sections.heading: Virgo strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Virgo's strengths are competence and care combined. It is thorough, dependable and unusually good at practical problems, often catching errors everyone else missed. An analytical mind lets it break a daunting task into manageable steps. The Maiden is usually modest and willing to do the unglamorous work that keeps everything running. It often holds a firm sense of ethics, and its advice tends to be specific and usable rather than vague. Many Virgos are lifelong learners who refine a skill over decades. Beneath the reserved surface sits real warmth, expressed through acts of service: fixing, organising and making life easier for the people around it.

Perfectionism is the classic Virgo trap. High standards can curdle into harsh self-criticism, endless revisions and anxiety about getting every detail exactly right. That critical eye may also turn outward, so corrections meant helpfully land as judgement. Worry is common, particularly about health, work or small things that may never matter. Relaxing does not come easily while something remains to be improved. The Maiden sometimes undervalues itself too, downplaying achievements and hanging back in the background. And because it prefers practical fixes, it can struggle simply to sit with a feeling, its own or someone else's, without reaching for a solution.

sections.heading: Virgo in love and relationships
paragraphs: Virgo tends to show love through attention and service. It remembers how a partner takes their tea, notices when they seem worn out and quietly handles the chores that make the week easier. It may be reserved at first, wary of vulnerability and slow to trust, but once committed it is devoted and thoughtful. The Maiden offers stability, practical care and honest conversation. In return it hopes for someone who sees those quiet gestures, respects its need for order and is patient with its worries. Grand romantic displays matter less to this sign than consistency, kindness and sincere thanks for everyday effort.

Criticism, given or received, is the usual source of strain. Virgo may point out flaws as a form of care, yet a partner can hear only disapproval. Meanwhile the Maiden feels hurt when its efforts pass unnoticed. Worry can spill into the relationship as well. Framing feedback gently, pairing it with appreciation and agreeing that not everything needs fixing all ease the tension. A partner can help by naming what Virgo does well and offering reassurance before it is requested. Taurus and Capricorn tend to share its values, while Cancer and Scorpio bring an emotional depth that softens its analytical edge.

sections.heading: Virgo at work
paragraphs: Virgo excels in work that rewards precision, analysis and service. Healthcare, editing, accounting, data analysis, administration, quality control, nutrition, engineering, technical writing, teaching and skilled craft all play to its strengths. It is often the colleague who makes systems actually function, catching mistakes and tightening processes. Clear expectations and the chance to master a discipline suit it well. As a leader, the Maiden leads by example, setting high standards and offering detailed, useful guidance. Colleagues tend to trust its judgement because it does its homework, checks its facts and rarely overpromises what it cannot deliver.

The pitfalls are perfectionism and overwork. Virgo can get stuck polishing details, struggle to delegate or take on too much because it believes it will do the job better itself. It may also undervalue its contribution and hesitate to ask for recognition or a pay rise. With money, this sign is usually careful, budgeting thoughtfully and comparing options before buying, though financial worry can still keep it up at night. Accepting "good enough" for low-stakes tasks frees energy for what truly matters. Speaking up for itself, clearly and calmly, helps the Maiden receive the credit its diligent work has long since earned.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Virgo decans
paragraphs: Virgo's growth edge is self-compassion. Its standards are an asset, but they become exhausting when applied without mercy. A useful practice is catching a self-critical thought and asking whether it would ever speak that way to a friend. Letting some tasks stay imperfect, especially in low-stakes corners of life, builds tolerance for uncertainty. Unhurried rest, such as walks, gardening or simple creative hobbies, quiets the analytical mind in a way scrolling never does. The Maiden also benefits from expressing feelings directly instead of channelling them into productivity. Finally, it grows by receiving help as graciously as it gives it, recognising that being cared for is not a burden but an ordinary part of closeness.

Virgo divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly August 23 to September 1, belongs to Mercury; the second, about September 2 to September 12, to Saturn; and the third, around September 13 to September 22, to Venus. Each has its own page, and every Virgo birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: Why are Virgos so critical?
faq.answer: Virgo is associated with analysis and improvement, so it naturally notices what could work better. Its criticism usually comes from a wish to help rather than to judge, though it can be hardest on itself. Gentle delivery and plenty of appreciation help balance the trait.

faq.question: What are Virgo's best qualities?
faq.answer: Virgos are often reliable, thoughtful, practical and genuinely helpful. They notice details, solve problems efficiently and show care through useful acts. Their modesty and integrity also make them trustworthy friends, partners and colleagues who can be counted on when it matters.

faq.question: What are the dates for Virgo?
faq.answer: About August 23 to September 22. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Virgo decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Mercury, the second (10° to 19°) with Saturn and the third (20° to 29°) with Venus, following the rulers of the earth signs in zodiac order.
